chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim from Aban from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to rule based on the testimony of one person along with the oath of the owner of the right.
ai.seo_question: What is the evidentiary requirement for a legal ruling when there is only one witness?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *shahadat al-wahid* (testimony of one witness) combined with the claimant's oath (*yamin*), a ruling attributed directly to the Prophet Muhammad. In Shia jurisprudence, this serves as a foundational mechanism for resolving disputes where full evidentiary proof is unavailable, emphasizing the judge's role in facilitating justice through flexible evidentiary standards. It underscores the practical application of prophetic tradition in maintaining social order and legal certainty within the community.
